articles.title: Cientos de aficionados, 13 jugadores de la sub-21 y un emotivo recuerdo a Jesús de Miguel en Las Rozas
articles.standfirst: Miles de personas acompañaron a la selección en la sesión de este lunes.
articles.summary: Miles de personas acompañaron a la selección en la sesión de este lunes.
articles.body: Ni el festivo, ni el fresquito, ni la lluvia pudieron con las ganas de los aficionados de la selección española de disfrutar de los campeones del mundo. Primero fueron las colas y, en cuanto se abrieron las puertas, llegaron las carreras de los más pequeños para ocupar los puestos de privilegio de las gradas, los que dan acceso a la foto y el autógrafo con el que tanto soñaban. La sesión se inició con los jugadores y el cuerpo técnico recordando la figura de Jesús de Miguel, por quien guardaron un emotivo minuto de silencio. Unai Simón portaba un ramo de flores y Ferran Torres una camiseta de la selección con el número y el dorsal del futbolista del Tenerife. Pese a la ausencia de jugadores de la talla de Lamine, quien se espera que esté disponible para el partido del domingo ante Inglaterra, los más pequeños -y los no tanto- animaron, cantaron y disfrutaron de los jugadores. Se trata de la última sesión abierta al público de este año. Un año en el que la selección se proclamó campeona del mundo. Por eso cientos de chavales ya lucían las dos estrellas en la camiseta que ahora acompañan con el autógrafo de su ídolo. En la sesión también participaron 13 jugadores de la selección española sub-21: Gonzalo García, Carlos Espí, Rodrigo Mendoza, Thiago Pitarch, Cristhian Mosquera, Manu González, Ángel Ortiz, Javi Hernández, Yarek Gasiorowski, David Mella, Pablo García, Bruno Iribarne y Salva Esquivel.

articles.title: Ben White: England defender says people don't know 'full story' behind his self-inflicted exile from national team
articles.summary: Arsenal defender Ben White says people don't know the "full story" behind his decision to previously make himself unavailable for England selection - but says he would make the same decision again.
articles.body:
Arsenal defender Ben White says people do not know the "full story" behind his decision to previously make himself unavailable for England selection - but says he would make the same decision again.

White, who has been named in Thomas Tuchel's squad for upcoming Nations League fixtures, left the Three Lions' camp at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar to return home for personal reasons.

He then made himself unavailable for selection for the rest of Gareth Southgate's reign, and was booed by some fans in March's 1-1 draw with Ukraine after returning to the squad under Tuchel.

Asked by BBC Radio 5 live's football correspondent John Murray what he would say to people who define his England career by what happened in Qatar, White said: "I think obviously people don't know the full story, because I [have] never said anything and I won't put anyone under the bus or share any of that.

"It's been amazing [though], obviously a bit tricky and not straightforward, but it is amazing to be here now."

White is now 29 and asked if he would have done anything differently in hindsight, he added: "No, I don't think I would.

"Obviously, I was a bit younger, I am a bit older now.

"I think as a person I am quite real and I think I made the decision that I would probably continue to make.

"So, one that I am not happy about, but obviously it happened and [it is] time to move on."

White came on for his first England appearance since 2022 in March's 1-1 draw with Uruguay and was booed by some supporters before he scored but also gave away the penalty that led to the visitors' equaliser.

After that, Chelsea midfielder Jordan Henderson said he and his fellow England players would always support White, while Tuchel said recently that the defender deserves "a new chapter" and "positive feedback from the crowd".

Asked how he dealt with the emotions of that night at Wembley, White added: "Before the game I was thinking 'don't not stand out, but [take it] nice and easy'.

"Then I came on and obviously got booed, then I scored, then I gave away a penalty.

"So, it was obviously full of emotions that night, [but] it was a good night."

England play Croatia at Wembley on Thursday, 12 November before taking on world champions Spain in Madrid three days later.

White is looking to add to his six England caps in this international break and said: "It is obviously an amazing privilege to be called up.

"The feeling is the same every time you do get this chance to play for England. It's one I am really looking forward to this week."

articles.title: Raúl, 32 años después
articles.summary: La opinión de Chisco García
articles.body: Seguro que ninguno de los presentes en el Carlos Tartiere aquella tarde del 6 de septiembre de 1994, cuando el Real Madrid de Jorge Valdano visitó Oviedo para disputar un amistoso relacionado con el fichaje de Robert Prosinecki, imaginó que, 32 años después, aquel joven delantero casi desconocido acabaría sentado en el banquillo azul. Era Raúl González Blanco, que empezaba a asomarse al primer equipo blanco y dejó su sello con un gol. El fútbol escribe historias que ni el mejor guionista inventaría. Raúl afronta ahora otro desafío: dirigir a un histórico que necesita recuperar su sitio en Primera división tras un año de frustración colectiva. No lo tendrá fácil, entre otras cosas porque muchos juzgarán al entrenador a través del recuerdo del delantero que tantas tardes de gloria dio al Real Madrid. Y son dos profesiones muy distintas. La figura de Raúl no puede generar más que ilusión. Quienes desconfíen de su contratación porque sólo ha entrenado en la cantera madridista, deberían valorar cuánto acumuló durante una de las carreras más brillantes de nuestro fútbol. Conoció técnicos de todos los perfiles, convivió con la máxima exigencia y aprendió a soportar la presión donde cada empate parece una derrota. De esas experiencias habrá extraído lecciones que ahora podrá trasladar al vestuario azul. El sábado, ante el Girona, empezaremos a descubrir cuánto hay del futbolista que fue en el entrenador que quiere ser. Jesús Martínez, presidente del Grupo Pachuca, nunca ha ocultado su preferencia por equipos ambiciosos, valientes y dispuestos a asumir riesgos. Tampoco su admiración por las grandes figuras del fútbol internacional. Raúl pertenece a ese grupo de elegidos. Por eso, la confianza de la propiedad parece casi ilimitada. Sólo una catástrofe de resultados podría quebrar una apuesta que va más allá de lo deportivo. Los clubes históricos necesitan ganar partidos, pero también que se reconozca su grandeza y que su nombre recupere el lugar que merece. Con Raúl, el Real Oviedo vuelve a cobrar protagonismo nacional e internacional. Se habla de los azules mucho más allá de Asturias y de nuestras fronteras. Es cierto que ahora las miradas estarán más pendientes del banquillo que del césped, pero quizá sea ahí donde empiece a construirse algo importante. 32 años después, aquel muchacho que comenzaba a escribir su leyenda de blanco regresa al Carlos Tartiere para intentar escribir otra historia. Esta vez, de azul. Y con toda la responsabilidad sobre sus espaldas.

articles.title: "Hoy la afición amarilla abraza a la blanquiazul"
articles.standfirst: Emotivo acto en memoria de Jesús de Miguel en la puerta 9 del Estadio de Gran Canaria
articles.summary: Emotivo acto en memoria de Jesús de Miguel en la puerta 9 del Estadio de Gran Canaria
articles.body: La rivalidad entre Las Palmas y Tenerife ha quedado a un lado para dar paso al cariño, el respeto y la unión del fútbol canario. Desde que falleció Jesús de Miguel, los clubes y sus aficiones han estado hombro sobre lágrima. Las aficiones de ambos clubes se han unido este lunes para rendir homenaje al futbolista, en un emotivo acto celebrado en la puerta 9 del Estadio de Gran Canaria, antes del encuentro que enfrenta al conjunto amarillo con el CD Eldense. Un gesto cargado de simbolismo, precisamente en la puerta que coincide con el dorsal que lucía el delantero tinerfeñista. En la puerta 9 se ha leído un manifiesto por la presidenta de Peñas de la UD Las Palmas, Guacimara Sosa. Un mensaje lleno de cariño y afecto con frases reseñables como "hoy la afición amarilla abraza a la blanquiazul porque la vida, el respeto y el dolor están por encima de nuestra rivalidad". Además de que Las Palmas hoy jugará con su tercera equipación (coincide con los colores del Tenerife), el club ha diseñado un brazalete especial para la ocasión. Un brazalete que portará el tinerfeño Kirian, y en el que figura el dibujo de Jesús de Miguel celebrando un gol, los escudos de la UD Las Palmas y el CD Tenerife y una frase que reza Jesús de Miguel siempre en nuestro recuerdo.

articles.title: El regalo de Militao a los hinchas del Valencia que increparon a Rüdiger tras el 0-2: "No hay que vivir con rencor"
articles.standfirst: El defensa madridista le dio su camiseta a dos aficionados que estaban tras el banquillo
articles.summary: El defensa madridista le dio su camiseta a dos aficionados que estaban tras el banquillo
articles.body: La goleada del Real Madrid en Valencia dejó varias escenas de tensión dentro del campo... pero también fuera. Y no sólo en la tangana que se montó en el descanso en el túnel de vestuarios. Tras el gol de Arda Güler, que significó el 0-2 del Real Madrid en ese momento en Mestalla, Antonio Rüdiger salió de su banquillo para celebrar el tanto de su compañero con efusividad, algo que no gustó a dos aficionados del Valencia que estaban situados justo detrás de los asientos de los suplentes madridistas. Ambos hinchas se lanzaron a increpar a Rüdiger por su celebración, mientras el alemán imitaba la celebración de Cristiano Ronaldo en una imagen bastante cómica. En otra acción del partido, tanto Rüdiger como Militao salieron del banquillo para quejarse de una decisión al juez de línea. Al volver a sus asientos, los mismos dos aficionados les indicaron de forma poco amistosa que se sentaran, señalándoles con el dedo. Tras el encuentro, esos dos mismos aficionados le pidieron a Militao su camiseta de calentamiento y el brasileño, sin dudarlo, acudió a la zona, se la quitó y se la regaló, a lo que los hinchas respondieron con alegría y golpes en el corazón para dar las gracias al madridista. Al hacerse viral el vídeo en redes, un usuario sacó la imagen de los dos hinchas preguntando: "¿Estos son los mismos 2 que le dicen absolutamente de todo a Antonio cuando celebra el gol?". Y ahí ha aparecido Militao para responder: "Si, no hay que vivir con rencor". Un gesto amable para cerrar otra visita picante a Valencia.

articles.title: Pierre Kalulu pulls out of France squad after picking up muscle injury vs. Fiorentina
articles.summary: A player who has played a ton of minutes this season is about to get a few weeks worth of rest — although not at his choosing.
articles.body:
We're less than one full day into the November international break and we have our first Juventus injury to report on. Not that we can necessarily blame international duty itself, but here we are with another Juve player injured and set to miss a little bit of time when club football resumes later this month.

Juventus announced on Monday that fullback/center back Pierre Kalulu will miss at least a couple of weeks — and likely a few games — after he reported muscle discomfort in his left thigh following the Bianconeri's 2-2 draw with Fiorentina at the Franchi on Sunday. Kalulu is expected to miss at least three weeks — the kind of thing that is at least somewhat easy to cope with considering Juve don't play again until Nov. 22 thanks to the international break. However, it is the latest in a string of injuries to important players that has been a constant theme of these first three months of the 2026-27 season.

If he is to miss at least the first week back from the international break, Kalulu won't be available for Juventus' games against Venezia and Omonoia FC in the Europa League, with there likely to be some nervy moments late fitness tests before the Bianconeri face Como on Nov. 29.

Here are the full details of things following Kalulu's visit to J Medical on Monday:

At the end of the match against Fiorentina, Pierre Kalulu reported muscle discomfort in his left thigh and underwent diagnostic tests this morning. The scans carried out at J|medical revealed a low-grade injury to his left biceps femoris. The player has begun treatment, in consultation with the French national team staff, who have withdrawn him from the squad.

At the end of the match against Fiorentina, Pierre Kalulu reported muscle discomfort in his left thigh and underwent diagnostic tests this morning.

The scans carried out at J|medical revealed a low-grade injury to his left biceps femoris. The player has begun treatment, in consultation with the French national team staff, who have withdrawn him from the squad.

OK, so just as Luciano Spalletti welcomes back Zeki Çelik into the squad, now we have to see Kalulu pull up with some sort of muscle injury that he was likely dealing with for at least some part of Sunday's draw with Fiorentina. It's a conveniently timed international break which will likely result in him not missing much actual game time, but it's yet another injury for Spalletti to deal with just as the schedule gets busy again. (Because, you know, playing every three or four days just feels like something that is sustainable four another four-week period. Good times.)

Çelik will likely slide back across the field and into his much more natural right back position if Spalletti chooses to play a back four coming out of the break. Where it gets interesting is if the three-man backline is the way Spalletti goes instead.

Either way, Juve will be without somebody in Kalulu who has played the most minutes this season of any player on the roster — including Guglielmo Vicario in goal — for at least a couple of games. Hopefully not much more than that.

articles.title: Liverpool Are Showing Interest In This Brighton Defender: What Will He Bring To Anfield?
articles.summary: In a recent report on the Daily Briefing, journalist Mark Brus mentioned that Liverpool are showing interest in Brighton and Hove Albion defender Luka Vuskov...
articles.body:
In a recent report on the Daily Briefing , journalist Mark Brus mentioned that Liverpool are showing interest in Brighton and Hove Albion defender Luka Vuskovic. It has been mentioned that the Reds are eyeing a move to recruit the Croat centre-back next year.

Vuskovic's Impressive Form In English Football

Vuskovic has enjoyed a good run of form at the English club this season as he has put in a series of impressive displays for them on the defensive end of the field. The 19-year-old has participated in 16 matches for Brighton in this campaign so far, scoring one goal and grabbing a couple of assists in multiple competitions.

The talented teenager is currently among the most gifted centre-backs in the Premier League . Thus, Liverpool would do well to lure him to Anfield next year.

His current contract at the American Express Community Stadium will run out in the summer of 2031, which could make it tough for the Reds to land him on a cut-price deal this January or at the end of this campaign.

MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 31: Luka Vuskovic of Brighton & Hove Albion reacts during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Manchester City and Brighton & Hove Albion at Etihad Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Matt McNulty/Getty Images)

Vuskovic is a good tackler of the ball and can sense the danger well to earn possession back for his team inside his half. He usually puts his foot through the ball when the opposition are on the front foot and can use his 1.93m frame to win a few 50-50 aerial duels for his team.

The Croat talent is also proficient at playing his way out from the back. Vuskovic is already quite familiar with the Premier League and won't take any time to adjust to life at the Merseyside club if they manage to get a deal done for him next year.

We can expect him to bring more quality and depth to Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola's defence. He is good enough to compete for a regular first-team spot at Anfield in the coming years.

At 19, the future looks quite promising for Vuskovic as long as he continues to improve with each year. He is undoubtedly a prospect to watch out for in the long run, so Iraola should focus on trying everything in his power to lure him to the Merseyside club this January or at the end of this campaign.

articles.title: Man United receive major Mauricio Pochettino lifeline as he eyes Michael Carrick’s job
articles.summary: Manchester United have been handed a golden opportunity to secure the services of Mauricio Pochettino as they weigh up Michael Carrick’s future.Pochettino’s...
articles.body:
Manchester United have been handed a golden opportunity to secure the services of Mauricio Pochettino as they weigh up Michael Carrick's future.

United's wild 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday has left Carrick far from safe , as questions over his suitability continue to linger.

While United's fightback in the face of adversity was admirable, the broader picture is considerably harder to ignore. The Red Devils sit in the relegation zone with just eight points, representing their worst start to a Premier League season ever.

Speaking to the press after the final whistle, Carrick made it clear that he expects to be in charge of the team after the international break.

A report covered by The Peoples Person relayed that the Old Trafford bosses are making their assessments as they consider whether or not to part ways with the legendary midfielder.

It was indicated earlier on Monday that Pochettino is among the candidates to succeed Carrick , with the Argentine open to taking the position. Pochettino has been strongly associated with the role previously, but no appointment has ever materialised, with United favouring alternative candidates.

Pochettino is currently leading the USMNT, having put pen to paper on a new record-breaking contract after a promising World Cup.

Beyond his interest in the role, United have received an additional lift.

Journalist Mike Keegan reports that Pochettino has a release clause that would let him leave his arrangement with the USMNT.

Keegan wrote on X, "Interesting to see Mauricio Pochettino's odds to become the next Manchester United manager slashed."

"He is contracted to the USMNT until the next World Cup but – perhaps importantly – there is a release clause in his deal."

"United previously looked into bringing Pochettino to Old Trafford but opted for Erik ten Hag instead. No decision yet on Michael Carrick – but should they opt for change then MP would tick a lot of boxes."

Others believed to be on the list are Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann.

Here are our ACC Power Rankings heading into Week 11 of the season.

The Hurricanes were finally defeated for the first time this season, but it doesn't change much for them in the College Football Playoffs.

Overlooked and disrespected, the Demon Deacons are the team that no one is talking about.

The Blue Devils have outscored their last two opponents 88-5. Things get tougher with this weekend's trip to Miami.

SMU hosts Wake Forest this Saturday in what is basically an elimination game for the ACC title.

The Cardinals have won four straight and look like they will go into the last week's matchup against Kentucky with a six-game winning streak.

It wasn't pretty, but the Tigers got it done in an 18-13 victory over Syracuse.

The Hokies took it on the chin at SMU on Friday night.

The Panthers had a bye week and travel to an ailing Florida State this Saturday.

The Tar Heels face a hot Louisville team this weekend.

It took some trick plays, but the Seminoles won their first game without Mike Norvell.

A bye week was precisely what the Cavaliers needed after three straight losses.

A two-game winning streak came to a screeching halt in a lopsided loss to Louisville.

It took one carry for the Wolfpack to learn how special Duke running back Nate Sheppard is. The rest of the game was just as big of a nightmare.

Things get difficult for Bill O'Brien's squad in the last three weeks with trips to Notre Dame and Miami on the schedule.

The Orange have a good chance at bowl eligibility with matchups against NC State and Boston College in the next two weeks.

The Golden Bears have lost five of their last six games.

articles.title: Konaté: "Para Mbappé no ganar el Balón de Oro fue duro, pero al día siguiente ya estaba tope"
articles.standfirst: El central del Real Madrid asegura que a nivel personal ha pasado su peor etapa y que vuelve a disfrutar
articles.summary: El central del Real Madrid asegura que a nivel personal ha pasado su peor etapa y que vuelve a disfrutar
articles.body: Ibrahima Konaté ha sido uno de los jugadores que ha aparecido en la zona mixta de Francia tras el primer entrenamiento en Clairefontaine del grupo de Zidane, que se mide a Italia en Milán el próximo jueves. El ex del Liverpool ha hablado del estado de Mbappé después de no haberse llevado el Balón de Oro. Deja claro que le ve muy bien y también destaca que él mismo se encuentra muy recuperado y a tope tras una campaña pasada complicada. "Kylian tiene una actitud fantástica, como se ha podido ver en los últimos partidos, en los que ha sido decisivo. Es muy importante para nosotros en Madrid. Es un competidor, así que, claro, no haber ganado el Balón de Oro cuando se lo merecía de sobra es duro, pero al día siguiente ya estaba a tope en el entrenamiento. Espero que esté en plena forma el año que viene para levantar el premio", aseguró Konaté. El central ha dejado claro que no está mejorando en estos últimos partidos sino que ya llegó al Madrid en condiciones para recuperar su mejor nivel tras una campaña pasada complicada, en la que la muerte de su padre o la de su compañero en el Liverpool Diogo Jota, en un accidente de tráfico en el que también falleció el hermano de éste, le afectó mucho. "No voy mejorando, y así ha sido desde el principio de la temporada. Todas las críticas del año pasado, aunque no siempre se haya mencionado lo extradeportivo a título personal, demuestran lo fuerte que soy mentalmente", ha añadido el jugador. El jugador del Real Madrid admite también el potencial del jugador del PSG Desiré Doué: "No me impresiona, pero el trabajo invisible que hace es sencillamente excepcional. Lo que hace es impresionante. Creo que aún le queda mucho para alcanzar su máximo potencial".

articles.title: Tom Brady leaves Birmingham: NFL legend and minority owner makes shock departure after three years
articles.summary: NFL legend and seven-time Super Bowl winner Tom Brady leaves Birmingham in surprise departure; Minority owner bought just over three per cent stake in St Andrew's club in August 2023 and leaves them top of Championship
articles.body:
In a statement, the club said: "Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years.

"It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom's experience and passion associated with the club, and the club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community."

No reason has been given for Brady's departure.

Brady, a seven-time Super Bowl champion in his playing days, bought a minority stake in the club in August 2023 during its takeover by an American capital management firm but saw the club relegated in his first season after the surprise sacking of John Eustace.

A summer of considerable spending, including the third-tier record £15m signing of England U21 forward Jay Stansfield, saw them promoted back to the Championship at the first time of asking before the club recorded a 10th-placed finish on their first season back in the second tier.

Brady leaves the club top of the table following Saturday's 2-1 win over Swansea following a run of seven wins from their last nine games.

articles.title: Las Palmas despierta a tiempo del letargo

articles.summary: Los canarios ganan con dos goles en el tiempo añadido
articles.body: Dos minutos de vértigo le bastaron a Las Palmas para llevarse los tres puntos ante el Eldense. Dos acciones de corazón en el tramo final de un partido que no tuvo demasiada historia debido a la incapacidad de ambos equipos para elaborar peligro. Pero ese creer fue lo que a la UD le otorgó el premio por el que especuló Calleja. La prueba está en que lo único reseñable de la primera parte fue el sentido homenaje para Jesús de Miguel. Ese minuto de parón fue el único que añadió el árbitro a un primer acto parco en intenciones y ocasiones. Se abrió más la segunda mitad y el Eldense sólo tardó diez minutos en llegar con peligro al área canaria para el golazo de Clemente que el colegiado acabaría anulando por fuera de juego. A la UD le costó atravesar el bloque defensivo del rival, realizando un fútbol lento en las transiciones, algo que recordó en más de una ocasión el público, silbando la pasividad ofensiva de su equipo. Fue Álex Suárez el que conectó un centro lateral de Iván Jaime dentro del área para salvar la papeleta de su equipo. articles.title: Tom Brady Leaves Birmingham City FC Ownership Group, NFL Legend Held Stake for 3 Years
articles.summary: Tom Brady is no longer part of the ownership group for Birmingham City FC.
articles.body:
Tom Brady is no longer part of the ownership group for Birmingham City FC.

The soccer team released a statement Monday revealing the NFL legend is leaving his role after three years.

"Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the Club over the last three years," the statement said. "It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom's experience and passion associated with the Club, and the Club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community."

As Sky Sports News pointed out, the timing is notable since Birmingham has played so well this season.

They sit atop the Championship League table with 29 points through 15 games thanks to eight wins, five draws and just two losses. They are tied in points with Middlesbrough and Stoke City but enjoy the advantage in goal-differential with a plus-14 mark.

The team's next game is Nov. 21 against Stoke City, which will go a long way toward determining early positioning in the race.

Birmingham City FC was in the Premier League for seven different seasons from 2002-03 through 2010-11 before spending the next 13 years in the Championship League. They then dropped down to League One in 2024-25 before playing their way right back up to the Championship the following season.

As for Brady, Birmingham City FC was not the only team he had an ownership stake in after his playing days.

He remains a limited owner of the NFL's Las Vegas Raiders despite working for Fox Sports as a color commentator.

The legendary quarterback is still best known for his playing career when he won seven Super Bowls for the New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He is the NFL's all-time leader in passing yards (89,214) and passing touchdowns (649) and is widely considered to be the greatest quarterback in league history.

articles.title: 'Aberdeen hunt yet another manager after ill-fated Robinson reign'
articles.summary: Stephen Robinson's tenure as head coach panned out as many Aberdeen fans feared it would, writes BBC Scotland's Liam McLeod.
articles.body:
Having covered the 4-0 home hammering by Hibernian on Saturday, it was clear there was no way back for Stephen Robinson as Aberdeen head coach.

The Northern Irishman looked like he would rather be anywhere else as the goals rained in on his team and he was duly sacked on Monday, less than eight months after taking charge.

Robinson's time at Pittodrie will not be remembered fondly by the club's supporters as he departs as the shortest serving full-time manager by games played.

He leaves the club second bottom of the Scottish Premiership, with the joint-worst attacking record in the division and with just three wins from 12 matches.

His appointment in March on a bumper three-and-a-half-year deal came after he had been under pressure at St Mirren. Despite winning the League Cup three months earlier, he had won just once in 13 Premiership outings.

Fans' eyebrows were raised at what was clearly a panicky appointment as Aberdeen dive-bombed towards a relegation play-off.

Robinson managed to keep the club in the top flight by scrambling a few wins towards the end of last season, but it has gone as many in the stands feared it would go this term.

Aberdeen sack Robinson after league slump

Yes, there have been huge changes to the squad, but there were massive changes at Falkirk as well and John McGlynn has led them to third, on a fraction of Robinson's budget. After Aberdeen shipped four at home, Falkirk put five past Hearts at Tynecastle.

The man who started the Hibs rout at Pittodrie was Jamie McGrath, who was allowed to leave Aberdeen on a free transfer in 2025, with the Dons unwilling to match the length of contract Hibs were offering.

McGrath's goal was an absolute stunner, arrowing into the top corner from distance. It was also symbolic of the mismanagement at his former club.

The problems at Aberdeen are deep-rooted and can mainly be traced back to chairman Dave Cormack's decision to replace the consistent Derek McInnes with Atlanta United's B team manager Stephen Glass in 2021.

McInnes' time was coming to an end anyway, but the club was in a decent place at the time and that appointment left people scratching their heads. Glass was gone less than a year later.

On 3 March, Cormack gave an in-house interview and spoke of sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel's "global" search for Jimmy Thelin's replacement

"For me, it's embarrassing that we're having to go through my sixth permanent appointment," he said. "We will take our time to get the right manager in place."

On 12 March, Robinson was appointed in the wake of a sobering capitulation at Dunfermline as their Scottish Cup defence came to an end. The parallels are obvious as Cormack hunts for yet another manager after yet another collapse.

The club has done brilliant work in the community and home attendances have never been so regularly high. There is undoubted potential at Pittodrie, but they have to get it right on the pitch.

In that same March interview, Cormack was bullish as he looked ahead.

"Make no mistake, we will be competitive next year," he said.

The club were eighth then. Less than eight months later, they sit 11th, two points off the bottom and six behind Dundee United in sixth.

It will not have escaped the attention of the club's fanbase that United manager Jim Goodwin - sacked by Cormack in 2023 after his own Hibs humiliation - is orchestrating some of the most attractive football in the top flight.

Aberdeen supporters do not have unrealistic expectations - despite what you may read elsewhere - but they do expect to not lose at home to Falkirk and St Johnstone or be hammered 4-0 at home by anyone. They would also expect to win more than one away league game in almost a year.

The money spent appointing managers, backing them and then sacking them has become eye-watering.

As Cormack, Pfannenstiel and new chief executive Adrian Bevington begin their search for yet another new manager, you can understand the supporters wondering how long the next incumbent will last, especially given how the squad assembled by Robinson disintegrated against Hibs.

Sandra: No hard feelings. Wish him well. Robinson got plenty wrong but shouldn't have been allowed to swap out a whole squad in his first gig at this level. The turnover of managers since our chairman came in is no coincidence, we are a shambles and I have no idea who could come in and sort this.

Mango: A club like Aberdeen should not be sitting 11th in the table but it has been coming for a few seasons. The board have allowed this to happen by letting our best players go and not reinvesting properly in established players. Robinson wanted these signings and his style of management was like a pressure cooker. He made rash tactical decisions and his game plan for most games did not work. I do heavily criticise the board. This next appointment will either make or break the club I've supported for over 25 years.

Niall: The enormity of the Aberdeen job was a step too far for Robinson. His opening remarks of building an attacking team with high press never materialised. Unfortunately, his successor will inherit another group of players low on quality, direction and confidence. Some of the blame must also lie with the recruitment team who have, once again, not delivered to an acceptable level. The next appointment needs to be much stronger to rebuild everything that is lacking just now but a huge task lies ahead given that the squad has already been rebuilt for this season following the Thelin debacle.

Greg: Was a panic appointment, but let's not forget what made the board panic was that they couldn't convince any of their preferred candidates to take the job. Got to wonder why a few top names took a look in the door and bolted.

Graeme: Gutted for Robinson. I think he should have been given more time. We need stability and we can't keep sacking managers. Aberdeen have been a bottom-six team since they got rid of McInnes. We seem to turn decent managers into poor managers, then we sack them, they go elsewhere and are given time to prove themselves and thrive at another club. We have to get the next appointment right, let's try to entice John McGlynn or Neil Lennon.

articles.title: El único refugio de Endrick
articles.standfirst: El joven delantero apenas encuentra minutos en el Real Madrid y vuelve a mirar a su selección para ganar ritmo y confianza
articles.summary: El joven delantero apenas encuentra minutos en el Real Madrid y vuelve a mirar a su selección para ganar ritmo y confianza
articles.body: Endrick necesita jugar y Brasil se ha convertido en su principal vía para conseguirlo. El joven delantero afronta un nuevo parón internacional con la posibilidad de sumar minutos lejos de Valdebebas, donde su protagonismo sigue siendo muy reducido. Por eso, Mourinho ha lanzado un mensaje directo a Carlo Ancelotti: quiere que el brasileño tenga oportunidades con su selección y estará encantado si el italiano se las da. "Mi opinión es clara, quiero que Endrick juegue. Si Ancelotti le hace jugar durante este parón internacional, estaré contento", reconoció el entrenador portugués después de la victoria ante el Valencia. Una petición que tiene un precedente muy significativo. En la última ventana internacional, el delantero participó en los tres encuentros de Brasil y disputó 65, 45 y 29 minutos, respectivamente. En total, 139 minutos con su selección. La comparación con su situación en el Madrid habla por sí sola. En sus ocho últimos partidos con el conjunto blanco, Endrick ha acumulado 136 minutos: se quedó sin jugar en dos ocasiones y, en los otros seis encuentros, participó durante 31, 69, 2, 5, 23 y 6 minutos. Es decir, ha jugado más con Brasil en tres partidos que con el Real Madrid en los ocho siguientes. Una diferencia que explica la importancia de este nuevo parón para el delantero y que deja una pregunta sobre la mesa: ¿cómo puede crecer y ganarse un sitio en el Real Madrid si no dispone de los minutos necesarios para demostrar su potencial? Mourinho, en cualquier caso, no quiere desprenderse de él. Pese a los rumores que sitúan a clubes como la Roma, el Milan o el Aston Villa detrás del brasileño de cara al mercado de invierno, el técnico ya dejó clara su postura: "Que se olviden, que se olviden. Si algún club interesado está esperando por Endrick, que lo haga sentado, porque se cansará de esperar". Y fue todavía más contundente al defender su continuidad: "Es un jugador al que adoro, que me encanta. Tiene un gran potencial y es muy importante para nosotros. Quien esté interesado en Endrick tendrá que luchar conmigo. No creo que necesite salir cedido, tendrá mucho éxito aquí". El portugués también explicó que el delantero llegó a su etapa en el equipo después de una lesión que le mantuvo apartado entre cuatro y cinco semanas. Incluso tenía previsto darle entrada ante el Villarreal, pero la expulsión de Vinicius y el desarrollo del encuentro cambiaron sus planes. Circunstancias que han retrasado su participación, aunque Mourinho insiste en que cuenta con él. Ahora, Endrick vuelve a mirar a Brasil. Los minutos que pueda sumar con Ancelotti serán importantes para recuperar ritmo competitivo y confianza antes de regresar a Madrid. Su reto será conseguir que esas buenas sensaciones también se traduzcan en más oportunidades con el Real Madrid. El desafío para Mourinho será encontrar la manera de integrar a Endrick en la rotación cuando vuelva la competición. El técnico ha frenado cualquier posibilidad de salida y ha reivindicado su talento, pero la mejor forma de demostrar esa confianza será darle espacio sobre el césped. Hasta entonces, Brasil seguirá siendo el escenario donde el delantero puede reivindicarse.

articles.title: Pólvora mojada en el Sabadell-Real Sociedad B
articles.standfirst: Los arlequinados encadenan la cuarta jornada sin ganar y el filial sale del descenso
articles.summary: El Sabadell encadenó la cuarta jornada sin ganar y la Real B sale del descenso
articles.body: El Sabadell y la Real Sociedad B firmaron tablas en la Nova Creu Alta (0-0). El Sanse tuvo las ocasiones más claras y perdonó, pero sale del descenso a la espera de los partidos aplazados. El equipo arlequinado encadenó el cuarto partido sin ganar, pero continúa invicto en casa y seguirá lejos de la zona roja. El Sabadell saltó al césped con ambición y en la primera mitad tuvo remató más (11-4) y con mayor peligro. Rahmani erró una ocasión muy clara, tras una pésima cesión de Beitia: Olasagasti estaba fuera de la portería, pero el delantero arlequinado disparó demasiado lejos y demasiado desviado. Justo después del minuto de homenaje a Jesús de Miguel, los locales perdieron a Quadri, sustituido por el protocolo de conmociones. La Real B inquietaba al contraataque y el Sabadell pudo marcar por mediación de Bonaldo y Pere Pons. En el minuto 36, el árbitro decretó penalti por manos de Beitia, pero corrigió a instancias del VAR. La segunda mitad fue más visitante: Soroeta disparó al larguero y Carrera marcó en su primer balón, pero estaba en claro fuera de juego. En el añadido, Adjabeng, solo en el punto de penalti, chutó fuera. El Sabadell pudo marcar en tres disparos de Joel Priego y un cabezazo de Bonaldo, pero ningún equipo halló el acierto.

articles.title: Nations League: Northern Ireland's Ceadach O'Neill ruled out of games against Ukraine and Hungary
articles.summary: Arsenal forward Ceadach O'Neill is ruled out of Northern Ireland's final two Nations League fixtures against Ukraine in Belfast and Hungary in Budapest.
articles.body:
Arsenal forward Ceadach O'Neill has withdrawn from the Northern Ireland squad for the forthcoming Nations League matches against Ukraine and Hungary because of injury.

O'Neill won his first senior cap against Guinea in June and came on as a late substitute in the Nations League wins over Georgia and Ukraine in the last international window.

The 18-year-old, who now has four international caps, recently made his first senior appearance for Arsenal, starting in the Carabao Cup last-16 tie against Fleetwood Town, which the Gunners lost in a penalty shootout.

O'Neill joins Sunderland defender Dan Ballard, Eoin Toal, and midfielders Ali McCann and Jamie McDonnell in being ruled out of the upcoming double-header because of injury.

Liverpool's Conor Bradley, who has not played since January, remains a long-term absentee.

Michael O'Neill's side are unbeaten at the top of League B2 with eight points from four matches and can earn promotion to the top tier for the first time.

Mee and Kenny handed first Northern Ireland call-ups

Kenny's background 'not that important' to O'Neill

Northern Ireland face Ukraine at Windsor Park on Saturday, 14 November at 19:45 GMT, before they travel to Budapest to play Hungary in their final match on Tuesday, 17 November.

Both games are live on BBC iPlayer and BBC Sounds.

Manchester United goalkeeper Dermot Mee and Portsmouth forward Eoin Kenny received their first call-ups to the NI squad for the games.

"We're naturally disappointed to be without Ceadach for the final two games of the campaign. He has been a great asset to the squad in the last international window and everyone here wishes him a swift recovery," said NI manager O'Neill.

"The wider squad and staff are looking forward to the two games ahead. We're in a good position in the group and there is plenty to play for.

"The Ukraine game in Belfast will be an important one for us, before we travel to Hungary for another challenging fixture. We'll be looking to build on the work we've done so far and finish the campaign strongly."

Northern Ireland are the only side left in the entire Nations League who have yet to concede a goal in this year's competition.

Shea Charles scored a last-gasp winner in Georgia in September before a goalless draw at home to Hungary.

A 3-0 victory over Ukraine was one of the most impressive performances from O'Neill's young side, and they ended the quadruple-header with another goalless draw, this time at home to Georgia.

If Northern Ireland can top the group they would not only win promotion to League A, but they would also be all but guaranteed of a play-off for Euro 2028.

articles.title: Should star Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith sit out the rest of the season after Buckeyes loss?

articles.body: The 2026 college football season seemed to set up perfectly for the Ohio State Buckeyes. They finished the 2025 regular season undefeated, only losing 13-10 to Indiana in the Big Ten Championship Game. While their College Football Playoff run ended with a disappointing 24-10 loss to the Miami Hurricanes, the Buckeyes entered the season as potentially the best team in the country. Julian Sayin returned for his second season as a starting quarterback. They returned a ton of talent on offense, including Bo Jackson and an experienced offensive line. While they'd have to replace talented defensive players like Caleb Downs, they brought back arguably the best player in college football, Jeremiah Smith. On the road against the Texas Longhorns, OSU entered the fourth quarter with a 23-3 lead. Through a series of miraculous, and frankly absurd outcomes, they lost 24-23. They recovered quickly, blowing out a solid Illinois team, and easily handling a very good Iowa Hawkeyes team on the road. On October 17 though, their season changed in the blink of an eye. In the process of handing Indiana their first loss in 23 games, Sayin suffered an arm injury while being tackled to the ground. While head coach Ryan Day was initially noncommittal, over the bye week news broke that Sayin would miss the rest of the season. And in the world of superconferences, timing is everything. The Buckeyes' first test with Luke Fahey as a starting quarterback was on the road against a very good USC Trojans team. They lost, 30-18, in a game that wasn't really that close. Fahey wasn't awful, wasn't outstanding, but the OSU defense wasn't effective against Jayden Maiava, and a litany of penalties doomed the Buckeyes. Their next game? Against the Oregon Ducks, another team with high-end talent struggling to live up to expectations. By November 7, their season had gone off the rails, murmurs of discontent with Day had started to circle around the fanbase, and OSU's playoff aspirations are on life support. If not already dead. Perhaps the bigger question? What happens now with Jeremiah Smith. One analyst, former NFL running back Damien Harris, thinks Smith is done at OSU. Particularly after how he reacted during the loss to the Ducks. "We just watched Jeremiah Smith play his last snap at Ohio State. He's done," he said while speaking on CBS Sports. articles.title: Tom Brady: NFL great ends association with Birmingham City
articles.summary: NFL legend Tom Brady ends his association with top-of-the-table Championship side Birmingham City after three years.
articles.body:
NFL legend Tom Brady has ended his association with top-of-the-table Championship side Birmingham City.

The seven-time Super Bowl champion became a minority owner in the St Andrew's club in August 2023 when he "entered a partnership" with club owners Knighthead Capital Management LLC.

Part of Brady's role involved him being chairman of an advisory board at Birmingham, with the club saying he would be "both investing [as well as] committing his time and extensive expertise" following his arrival.

However, the Blues announced his exit , external with a statement headlined 'Tom Brady departure'.

They added: "Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years.

"It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom's experience and passion associated with the club, and the club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community."

Former quarterback Brady, a three-time NFL most valuable player, retired in February 2023 after 23 seasons in the NFL, having won six of his Super Bowl titles with the New England Patriots and one with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Following the end of his playing career, he also acquired a stake Las Vegas Raiders, while also becoming part of the ownership group of the WNBA's Las Vegas Aces.

On top of that, Brady's commitments also include him being a lead NFL analyst for Fox Sports.

He leaves with Birmingham top of the Championship on goal difference with 29 points after 15 games.

articles.title: Michael Carrick: Manchester United expected to sack head coach
articles.summary: Michael Carrick's Manchester United reign appears close to an end following the club's worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years.
articles.body:
Manchester United look increasingly likely to sack head coach Michael Carrick.

The club opted to stick with Carrick after the side's 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on 25 October, with the intention of reassessing the situation during this month's international break.

Multiple sources have told BBC Sport that the board remain committed to that process, and that no final decision on Carrick's future has been made.

However, there is a growing expectation that chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox will recommend to minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family for Carrick to be sacked.

The 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday means United, who are 18th in the table, have made their worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years.

BBC Sport reported in October that the club had sounded out former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann over replacing Carrick.

Former Chelsea coach Antonio Conte is known to be keen on the role, while multiple sources have told BBC Sport that former Spurs boss Mauricio Pochettino is open to a move to Old Trafford.

Pochettino signed an extension to his contract as USA coach in August.

However, the deal is thought to contain clauses that would allow him to leave for specific high-profile jobs. The US have a two-legged Concacaf Nations League play-off with Haiti on 14 and 18 November.

The Villa draw was Carrick's third match in charge since the club opted to give the 45-year-old more time at Old Trafford.

Results during that time - a win, a draw and a defeat - were mixed, and displayed the best and worst of Carrick's reign with United shipping goals but displaying good character to come back from two goals down on three occasions.

United's board toyed with sacking Carrick after the loss to Bournemouth, but decided the Englishman - and his players - had earned the opportunity to show that they could turn the club's fortunes around.

It was also felt that the two-week international break in November represented a better chance for the club to properly assess the club's start to the campaign.

Unfortunately for Carrick, it makes for poor reading.

With one victory in 10 Premier League matches, United have made their worst start to a top-flight campaign since the 1986/87 season.

They sit 18th in the table, one point above bottom-placed Crystal Palace.

Only the Eagles and Ipswich have conceded more than the 19 goals United have shipped in the Premier League this season.

It is hard to believe given the club's current predicament just how quickly Carrick's tenure has soured.

How did it unravel so quickly for Carrick?

Looking back, the 48 hours before United's season-opening match at Hull were pivotal.

With Benjamin Sesko still trying to ease his way back from the shin issue that ended his previous campaign early, Amad Diallo suffered an ankle injury that would rule him out for seven weeks. It meant Carrick was deprived of his first-choice striking alternative, with Bryan Mbeumo having to play on the right of the attack.

Carrick instead turned to Matheus Cunha, whose preference for dropping deep took him into the spaces captain Bruno Fernandes likes to occupy.

It neutralised United's attack on a day they seemed ill-prepared to meet the physical challenge of an opponent motivated by their long-awaited Premier League return.

In his role as interviewer for Nordic broadcaster Viaplay, former Norway and Middlesbrough striker Jan Aage Fjortoft later claimed United had lacked passion - something Carrick dismissed as "ridiculous".

"It's one game," Carrick told the media afterwards.

The following week, United were losing to Ipswich - another newly promoted side. Only a slip from Marcelino Nunez inside his own half allowed Cunha to tee up Fernandes for an undeserved equaliser.

The Portugal playmaker, who had just been crowned PFA Player of the Year for 2025-26, went on to complete a hat-trick in a 5-2 win.

He has scored just once - a penalty against Villa on Sunday - in the league since.

After the Ipswich win came a trip to Everton.

Twice United led, the second occasion when Sesko struck two minutes from full-time after coming on as a substitute. Deep into stoppage time, Ainsley Maitland-Niles drove home from long range to deny the visitors.

Asked how confident he was in his side's ability to react to a disappointing start to the season, Carrick snapped back: "It's not been that bad."

Time and again, United's fitness was called into question. They struggled badly against a Manchester City side reduced to 10 men in the first half before their rivals benefited from an Erling Haaland goal that referees' chief Howard Webb later admitted should not have stood.

Carrick's complaints were justified - but they masked a poor performance from his team.

After taking a 2-0 lead inside 10 minutes against Brighton in the EFL Cup, United were outplayed and beaten, thanks to two goals in four second-half minutes.

The fine margins United benefited from during Carrick's interim spell were now going against them, and his coaching staff - lauded months earlier - could not find an answer.

Carrick called Cunha's injury-time equaliser against a Fulham side who started the game bottom of the table a positive to build on. But immediately after the international break, United were held to another draw - conceding in injury time to an out-of-form and 10-man Tottenham.

The whirlwind was starting to pick up strength.

Lisandro Martinez, who scored an own goal against Fulham, was at fault for Spurs' leveller, which made his post-match outburst after the 2-0 Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid more amazing.

The Argentina defender criticised United's summer recruitment and placed the blame at the door of "the technical director" - Wilcox.

By the time of Martinez's outburst, Sesko and left-back Luke Shaw were injured. Marcus Rashford has not played since. The rotation at left-back that eventually led to Carrick starting five different players in that role was in full swing.

After conceding in the opening minute against Atletico, Como scored inside the first two in a 4-1 Champions League defeat for United. Fernandes came out afterwards and criticised Carrick's tactics.

He was dropped for the Bournemouth game, but returned as captain at Chelsea. United were beaten in both matches.

With just three wins in 15 matches in all competitions this season and United stuck in 18th in the Premier League, Carrick is set to pay the price.

articles.title: Michael Carrick future: Man Utd head coach position increasingly in doubt but no final decision made
articles.summary: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick's position under increasing threat but no final decision made despite worst-ever Premier League start and dropping into relegation zone with Sunday's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa
articles.body:
As reported earlier on Monday, the club is carrying out a full review of the team's performance so far this season, led by director of football Jason Wilcox, with a plan for a decision to be made before the end of this international break.

Carrick was given a reprieve following the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth a fortnight ago, with the bosses keen to give him a further three matches to try to turn the team's fortunes around.

But the pressure has continued to mount on Carrick after an eighth straight Premier League match without a win. There are now real doubts about whether he will be in charge of the team which goes to Anfield to play Liverpool the weekend after next.

The United hierarchy is determined that results have to improve, but they want to be sure about which direction to take the team before any action is taken.

If they decide to remove Carrick from his position, they want to avoid having an interim head coach take over, but as yet, there have been no substantive talks with other potential candidates.

Sky Sports News understands the club's hierarchy are planning to use the international break to fully evaluate the season so far and reassess their options.

Carrick and the players have all had Monday off after rescuing a late point against Villa on Sunday, but the head coach and his staff are due back into Carrington on Tuesday.

With most players away on international duty and no first-team training sessions planned in the coming days, that has bought some breathing space for a full re-evaluation of the season.

One win in 11 games, 30 goals conceded so far in all competitions, the worst record of any team in the top-five European leagues, and a worst-ever start to a Premier League season has ramped up the pressure on Carrick.

Those problems have outweighed the positivity brought about by the comebacks of the last two matches.

It is thought the United hierarchy feel Carrick over-achieved last season, with a third-placed League finish earning Champions League football.

But it is equally clear the bosses are adamant that the club's current crop of players have woefully under-achieved so far this season.

Sky Sports News understands there are three key reasons why United are not rushing a decision over the head coach position - all of which have given Carrick an extended stay of execution.

Firstly, the supporters are not singing for him to be sacked. It is unlikely that will ever happen, such is the affection of the fanbase for a legendary player who won 11 major trophies with United, including the Champions League and five Premier League titles.

As such, the pressure to change the boss which other clubs often experience from the stands has not materialised at Old Trafford.

Secondly, there is a feeling in the boardroom that Carrick and his coaching staff still retain the support of the players.

Despite the chaotic nature of the last two games, they have produced a Champions League win against Roma and a draw against a good Villa side - with notable comebacks in both.

As such, the assessment seems to be that the players have not downed tools, and they are still fighting for Carrick.

Thirdly, United's bosses remain unconvinced at this stage that changing the head coach will solve the team's problems.

If they did believe that, they could have already made a move to sack Carrick and appoint a candidate such as Julian Nagelsmann or Eddie Howe - both of whom are out of work, available, and thought to be keen to talk to United if a vacancy becomes available.

'It doesn't matter who's in charge at Man Utd'

Sky Sports News chief reporter Kaveh Solhekol :

"The club needs to become Manchester United again. They need to turn into a club who are capable of winning the title regularly, winning the European Cup again.

"It doesn't matter who's in charge, in my opinion. You could have Carlo Ancelotti, Pep Guardiola or Jurgen Klopp. But with the present ownership structure, I don't think things are going to change.

"You could bring in another manager but you would just paper over the cracks. We're talking about a club that used to rub shoulders with Barcelona and Real Madrid.

"If things carry on as they are at the moment, they'll be rubbing shoulders with Lincoln and QPR. There's a circus around the club, everyone talking about what's going wrong and how it can be changed.

"But I think most Man Utd fans think that unless you change the owners, nothing is going to change."
authors: Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett and Danyal Khan

articles.title: Manchester United's Michael Carrick Expected to Be Fired as Manager, New Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: Change is coming to Manchester United.
articles.body:
According to David Ornstein, Adam Crafton and Laurie Whitwell of The Athletic , the club is "expected to relieve" manager Michael Carrick of his duties.

Per that report, "The club continue to insist that no decision has been reached but multiple sources, speaking to The Athletic on the condition of anonymity to protect relationships, indicate work has been undertaken on potential replacements and the anticipation is a change will be made before the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool in 13 days' time."

USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino "would be expected to figure highly among the candidates," per that report, while Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann "have admirers at the club."

Carrick, 45, replaced Ruben Amorim in January on an interim basis and was appointed to the full-time gig in May after leading United to 11 wins across 16 matches, with the club finishing third on the Premier League table and earning a berth in the Champions League.

But the 2026-27 campaign has been an abject disaster. Manchester United currently sit 18th on the table with just eight points through 10 matches, a stunning run of mediocrity for the proud club.

Manchester United have had a revolving door of managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013, with 11 different men holding the gig as caretakers or on a full-time basis. The Red Devils haven't won a Premier League title in that time, which has also coincided with the unpopular ownership of the Glazer family (Jim Ratcliffe leading football operations was supposed to help in that regard, though the returns to this point haven't been promising).

The constant turnover at manager, paired with inconsistent approaches to roster-building and a general sense of dysfunction within the club have led to a sustained period of United finding themselves trailing far behind Premier League powers like Arsenal, Liverpool, Chelsea and Manchester City (115 charges notwithstanding) over the past two decades.

That's the context the next manager will have to shoulder as he hopes to right the ship.

articles.title: Jordon Hudson Sues Airbnb Hosts over Doorbell Camera Video of Shirtless Bill Belichick
articles.summary: BOSTON (AP) — Jordon Hudson is suing two Airbnb hosts over a doorbell camera video of a bare-chested Bill Belichick, saying that the 2023 clip invaded her privacy by ultimately prompting public disclosure of her relationship with the Super Bowl-winning coach.
articles.body:
BOSTON (AP) — Jordon Hudson is suing two Airbnb hosts over a doorbell camera video of a bare-chested Bill Belichick, saying that the 2023 clip invaded her privacy by ultimately prompting public disclosure of her relationship with the Super Bowl-winning coach.

Hudson, who went on to become a public presence by Belichick's side, says in the lawsuit that they were keeping their romance private when they stayed at the Boston-area rental in the summer of 2023. Then the doorbell video — which showed him stepping, shirtless, out of the home onto a porch — emerged that fall and made media rounds.

Hudson wasn't in the video, but she ultimately was publicly identified as the paramour of the former New England Patriots and current University of North Carolina head coach, who is almost 50 years her senior. Her lawsuit accuses rental hosts Elise McDevitt and Craig Nolan of leaking the footage and personal information about her.

"These egregious violations of Ms. Hudson's privacy have, among other things, resulted in significant unwanted publicity and scrutiny of Ms. Hudson and her relationship with Mr. Belichick" and have subjected her to ridicule, attorney Howard Cooper and colleagues wrote in a complaint filed Friday in Massachusetts.

Voicemail and email messages seeking comment were left Monday for McDevitt and Nolan, and a social media message was sent to McDevitt. No attorney is listed for them yet in the court record.

Belichick isn't part of the lawsuit. Messages seeking comment from him were left for a UNC football team spokesperson. At a recent news conference, Belichick, 74, wouldn't answer a question about whether he was still in a relationship with Hudson, 25.

Belichick was nearing the end of his 24-year, six-time-Super Bowl-winning tenure as the Patriots' head coach when he and Hudson spent time at the Airbnb she booked in Winthrop, according to her lawsuit. It says she learned of the video when McDevitt texted it to her along with an instruction not to park in front of a neighbor's house.

In subsequent texts, McDevitt joked about football and said it was "clear who is on the video," and Hudson repeatedly pressed her to delete it, according to the lawsuit. It says McDevitt eventually said she'd trash the footage but hedged that "videos are never totally deleted," adding that she was "not distributing the video."

After the clip emerged on the social platform X in November 2023, McDevitt denied having posted it or leaked it to anyone, the lawsuit said. But McDevitt later texted that she "had sent it to a few people" but never envisioned it becoming public, according to the complaint.

Messages were left Monday for Airbnb, which isn't named in the lawsuit. It says the company kicked McDevitt and Nolan off the platform after Hudson reported what had happened.

Juega mucho, tiene mucha calidad... Cuando él está en el campo, el equipo juega mejor y tenemos más juego asociativo. A mí es el que más me ha sorprendido". ¿Te ayuda más Diomande que Vinicius?: "No creo que me ayude más, creo que se ve más. Diomande hace una carrera para atrás y sale en todos los lados. Vinicius hace tres y luego hay una que no corre... y sale la que no ha corrido. Si Vini marcase tres goles por partido nadie le diría nada... Lo más importante para nosotros es que vuelva al máximo nivel porque si está en su 'prime' tenemos un equipazo". "Vinicius es un jugador que lleva cinco años jugando a un nivel espectacular, se puede entender que ahora tenga una mala racha. Yo veo que tiene ganas y en el entrenamiento lo intenta, que es lo importante", dijo Marc en defensa de su compañero. Un nuevo Real Madrid: "Al principio no tuvimos mucha pretemporada, entrenador nuevo, casi no pudimos entrenar... ¿Si corremos más ahora? No lo sé, quizá elegimos mejor los momentos o estamos más compactos y da la sensación de que somos unas bestias, pero creo que tampoco hemos cambiado tantas cosas". El Clásico y Lamine: "¿Lo que dijo Lamine de que me iba a comer? No tengo que decir nada. A mí no me gusta hablar o fardar, me gusta estar calladito y hacer mi trabajo. Me salió un buen partido y seguramente me tocará jugar muchos partidos contra él, me tocará sufrir y él se llevará los méritos..." Mourinho: "La imagen es diferente, para bien. Es muy cercano, muy buena persona, le gusta mucho hablar. No necesita dar charlas de media hora, en cinco minutos te dice lo que necesitas". Maffeo: "Yo sé cómo es Maffeo... y yo soy también un poco así. Es muy intenso, muy cabra loca... pero luego estuvimos hablando y muy bien. En el partido es como muy pesado, muy intenso, bastante odioso, pero luego al terminar el partido ya se ha acabado". Su tatuaje de De la Fuente: "No me arrepiento, pero ya no me hago más, yo ya no me meto en fregados... Mourinho me mandó una foto con mi pecho y su cara tatuada". Señalado en Alemania: "No sé, lo han pagado conmigo y sé que en Alemania no puedo jugar".

articles.title: Ole Miss Fined $250K by SEC After Viral Video of Fans Throwing Debris on Field in Loss to Georgia
articles.summary: Ole Miss will pay a lofty fine after its fans threw debris on the field during a blowout loss to Georgia on Saturday.
articles.body:
Ole Miss will pay a lofty fine after its fans threw debris on the field during a blowout loss to Georgia on Saturday.

The SEC announced Monday that the school has been fined $250,000 for its fans' actions during the game. The penalty falls under the "sportsmanship, game management and alcohol availability policies" established by the conference.

Frustrations were already mounting for fans in the second quarter when they trailed 21-0, and an overturned Rebels' interception only led to more ire from the student section.

Things boiled over after a pass interference call against Ole Miss, and fans responded by pelting the field at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium with trash and debris. It led to a nearly 10-minute delay.

While it wasn't quite as much trash as other schools have thrown on the field in recent years, it was enough to warrant a fine.

The SEC Bylaws and Commissioner's Regulations state: "If cans or plastic bottles are used as projectiles or otherwise cause game management issues, the institution is subject to an immediate fine and suspension of the alcohol sales privilege."

The SEC said that it will not revoke Ole Miss' right to sell alcohol at football games, "but reserves the right to do so in the future."

Taking on Georgia has been a costly ordeal for the Rebels in recent years, though for very different reasons. After Ole Miss upset Georgia in 2024, the school had to pay a $350,000 fine because fans stormed the field.

The Rebels dropped to 6-3 with the loss as their College Football Playoff hopes continue to dwindle. Georgia, meanwhile, perhaps established itself as the best team in the country by picking up its third ranked win of the season.

articles.title: College Football Playoff committee executive admits they don't care fans are against 24-team playoff
articles.summary: The College Football Playoff expands to 24 teams by 2027-2028, but Executive Director Rich Clark acknowledged fans overwhelmingly oppose the change.
articles.body: Monday made what was long rumored official: we're moving to a 24-team College Football Playoff starting in the 2027-2028 season. The reaction from most fans, commentators, analysts as well as many coaches and people within the sport, can be summed up in one word: why? As recently as 2023, the playoff was four teams. The smaller field ensured that the best of the best would compete for a title. Only one-loss or undefeated teams had a chance at postseason glory ... well, unless you were an undefeated Florida State team. COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF EXPANDING TO 24 TEAMS IN 2027, WITH MORE GAMES COMING TO CAMPUSES ACROSS THE COUNTRY Then, in 2024, we moved to a 12-team format, which offered more opportunity for teams to change their season. The 2024-2025 Ohio State Buckeyes were a perfect example, losing the final game of the season before roaring back to life and steamrolling their way through to a championship. The 12-team format has generally been well liked; it's a solid balance of maintaining the exclusivity of the tournament, while adding more big postseason games on campuses and mostly preserving bowl season and the importance of the regular season. While the upcoming 2026-2027 version of the playoff will be just the third under the expanded format, we're already moving on to even more teams. Somehow. 24 teams essentially means the end of meaningful bowl games. With a bowl field so diluted by the increase in playoff participants, the remaining bowls will be picking up scraps. Major conference championship games are set to become a thing of the past. The regular season, long the best in sports, will be significantly less meaningful. Not only will three losses not be enough to keep teams out, there's a strong chance that four or potentially even five loss teams (from the SEC) will be in the 24-team playoff. This might mean more scheduled games between big programs, since they'll no longer be concerned about a single loss hurting their chances, but if it doesn't, the sport will have sacrificed the regular season almost entirely. Which again, raises the all-important question: who wanted this? Who was asking for it? Why is it even happening? The answer is money, money and money. The Big Ten led the charge for more playoff spots, and other conferences and groups eventually fell in line. The SEC, long the hold out, caved, presumably because commissioner Greg Sankey realized he could start campaigning for all 16 conference teams to reach the playoff each season. Obviously, more playoff games means more money coming from the broadcast partner, ESPN. More teams will have late-season home games with a potential "playoff appearance" on the line. Then be able to sell expensive home playoff game tickets to their fans. Coaches now have a lower bar to claim a successful season. And boosters can see a return on investment instead of seeing their money go towards reaching the Pop-Tarts Bowl. The one group missing here? Fans. As usual. Fans weren't asking for this, and surveys have shown that they overwhelmingly don't want it. Unsurprisingly, it's happening anyway. And in a news conference announcing the change, Executive Director Rich Clark explained why: the playoff committee doesn't care. BIG TEN CONFERENCE COMMISSIONER GIVES TONE DEAF STATEMENT ABOUT 24-TEAM COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF Clark said on the call that changes brought about by the 24-team field will be beneficial for the sport, and most importantly, the business school executive's new favorite word: "stakeholders." "New scheduling standards will incentivize institutions to schedule more compelling non-conference matchups during the regular season, and 16 Playoff games will now be played on campuses, bringing Playoff football to more students and local fans," Clark said. "Finally, our commitment as the CFP administration and staff, we will make the 24-team Playoff spectacular for the fans, for the student-athletes, for the institutions, and for all our stakeholders." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Clark answered a few questions, saying that the committee will evaluate and encourage strong schedules, and teams will be required to play 10 games against teams from Power 4 conferences. That's all well and good. But what came next was frustrating and a bit emblematic of how this whole process has played out. One reporter asked Clark about fan opinion, saying "the online segment of the fan base seems to be maybe against this," and wondered how Clark thought it would be "received by fans." Here's what he said: "We're aware of the fan sentiment and that many fans aren't in favor of expansion," Clark responded. "That was certainly weighed into the decision. It was considered. Ultimately we just need to make a spectacular Playoff. I mean, the CFP has a responsibility to our fans, they're the lifeblood of college football. We owe it to them to make this great. That really is our intent. We appreciate our fans. We did take into account their sentiment. That was rolled into this decision. But we decided to move forward with it." Ah. Yes. We know fans don't want it, we just didn't care and did it anyway because it made more money. Perfection. Obviously, that's the real explanation for why they decided to "move forward" anyway. Fans are dead last when it comes to priorities among the leadership in college football. A "spectacular playoff" doesn't require 24 teams, in fact, it's more likely to dilute it. In 2025-2026, for example, several games between P4 and G6 teams were widely decried as being non-competitive. Ole Miss blew out Tulane 41-10 and Oregon handled James Madison 51-34. Even in the 2024-2025 playoff, ESPN's Kirk Herbstreit went on a rant decrying the Indiana Hoosiers reaching the 12-team field when they lost 27-17. In a 24-team format, how bad will that 24th team be? SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Probably not great! OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD But this is what happens in modern college football; those in charge focus exclusively on short-term financial success over long-term health. Fans come last. Money comes first. At least this time they're admitting it.

articles.title: Urban Meyer Calls Out Elimination of Conference Title Games with CFP Expansion, 'Breaks my Heart'
articles.summary: Some of Urban Meyer's most memorable wins of his legendary college football coaching career came in conference championship games, and he isn't happy those contests are disappearing next season.
articles.body:
Some of Urban Meyer's most memorable wins of his legendary college football coaching career came in conference championship games, and he isn't happy those contests are disappearing next season.

"Yeah, it breaks my heart," he said on The Triple Option , which is an AMP Sports Original Series (57:41 mark). "But, now it's conference champion. You know, people are going to get rings, but they don't deserve them… because no one's going to really win outright probably."

His comments came after the College Football Playoff announced it is expanding from 12 teams to 24 starting with the 2027-28 campaign. As part of that expansion, there will no longer be conference championship games for Power Four schools.

What's more, the new playoff format will feature a first-round bye for the top eight seeds and an additional round of home games on campus:

But Meyer was focused on the loss of the conference title games.

"I'm going to go on record again," he said. "There's nothing other than the big one. There's nothing more rewarding than when you go on the field in front of a giant crowd and you go play for your conference championship and afterwards they give you the trophy and you get a ring. For those who say 'come on'—you haven't played any. You probably haven't coached in it."

Meyer would know better than most what it is like to win on such a stage.

He coached Florida for six seasons from 2005 through 2010 and reached the SEC Championship Game three times. He won it in 2006 over Arkansas and parlayed the momentum from that into a national title before the Gators faced Alabama in back-to-back conference championship games in 2008 and 2009.

Those were the Florida teams with Tim Tebow under center, and the Gators outlasted the Crimson Tide in the first one and then went on to win another national title. Yet Alabama got revenge in 2009 and won its own national title after that victory.

Meyer's conference title game success didn't stop at Florida.

He led Ohio State to the Big Ten Championship Game four times in a six-year span from 2013 through 2018. Meyer's Buckeyes won the conference title in three of those years, including in 2014 when third-string quarterback Cardale Jones directed a stunning 59-0 victory over Wisconsin.

Ohio State reached the CFP in large part because of that performance and then went on to beat Alabama and Oregon to win the national championship.

Meyer has plenty of favorable memories in conference championship games and isn't pleased other coaches and players will miss out on such an opportunity moving forward.

articles.title: Urban Meyer Sends Stern Warning to Jeremiah Smith After Going Off on Ohio State Coaches
articles.summary: Jeremiah Smith has been at the center of a storm since the Ohio State Buckeyes’ 41-28 loss to the Oregon Ducks on Saturday.The star wide receiver went viral...
articles.body:
Jeremiah Smith has been at the center of a storm since the Ohio State Buckeyes' 41-28 loss to the Oregon Ducks on Saturday.

The star wide receiver went viral after cameras caught him screaming toward the Ohio State sideline late in the third quarter. And the moment has divided Buckeyes fans and media members alike.

Now, the man who built the Ohio State program into a juggernaut is weighing in on what happened.

Former Buckeyes head coach Urban Meyer didn't rip Smith for his outburst. But he did make it clear the 20-year-old needs to be more self aware when it comes to his behavior.

Urban Meyer Has Strong Message for Jeremiah Smith

During a recent episode of "The Triple Option" podcast , Meyer was asked what he would do if he were still coaching Smith. His answer was more of a teaching moment than a scolding.

"I would probably call him in and sit down and talk to him — and I know Jeremiah but I don't know him," Meyer said. "I know him because of what coach Day, and the strength coach, and what everyone tells me about this kid. He's the perfect teammate, he's the perfect worker, he's got a lifestyle that there's no question marks to it.

"So, I'd call him in and just say, 'Realize the camera is on you as much as it is anyone else, probably anyone else in the United States of America. And he's earned that. So, just hustle back and don't let anyone start to question who you are.'"

In other words, Meyer isn't questioning Smith's character. He's simply warning him that one heated moment can quickly change the narrative about him.

Jeremiah Smith's Outburst Sparked a Heated Debate

It's not hard to understand why Smith was frustrated.

Ohio State jumped out to a 14-0 lead before Oregon scored 38 straight points. Smith went more than two full quarters without a catch. The grab that set him off late in the third quarter was his first since the opening quarter.

He still finished with seven catches for 133 yards and a touchdown. But most of that came after the game was out of reach.

"You cannot be the best player in the country and a captain and all of the things that Jeremiah Smith is and go stomping down the field like a petulant child," Jeremy Birmingham, who covers the Buckeyes for 97.1 The Fan, said on "Snap Judgments" after the game.

Smith didn't respond directly. But he made his feelings known by reposting a defense from former Buckeyes lineman LeCharles Bentley, who argued that Smith's frustration shouldn't be treated as proof of immaturity.

That's exactly the kind of conversation Meyer wants Smith to avoid.

Smith has 69 catches for 1,200 yards and 14 touchdowns this season. He's said this will most likely be his last in Columbus. With the Buckeyes (6-3) fighting to keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive, Ohio State is going to need him at his best, not as a viral clip.

articles.title: Vikings’ Adrian Peterson talks ‘huge’ honor joining Minnesota’s Ring of Honor
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings battled the Buffalo Bills at U.S. Bank Stadium on Monday Night Football as Carson Wentz got an endorsement from Jason Kelce. The Vikin...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings battled the Buffalo Bills at U.S. Bank Stadium on Monday Night Football as Carson Wentz got an endorsement from Jason Kelce . The Vikings and Bills were tied at three points each late in the first half as Kevin O'Connell's team narrowly avoided a kick return disaster .

The Bills finally punched in a touchdown as QB Josh Allen found Keleki Latu for a 25-yard pass-and-catch, obscuring a big honor given to Vikings legend Adrian Peterson .

Peterson was inducted into Minnesota's Ring of Honor, and spoke about the situation on the sidelines of the field alongside his mother Bonita Jackson. He became the 29th purple jacket to enter the prestigious ring.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"It's just a tremendous moment, it's huge, it's been a long time coming, it just makes me reflect back on my career and everything that led up to this moment, it's just special and it's a great accomplishment."

"I'm so proud of him, I'm so proud of this day…I'm happy to be here to share this moment with him."

Jackson announced that she would be announcing her son into the Ring of Honor, saying it would be "an honor and a privilege to do that."

"The fanbase is the best fanbase in the world," Peterson added. "Anytime I touch down here it's always love, and that's the one thing I appreciate and cherish the most."

The Vikings had 86 total yards of offense in the first half including 69 passing yards from the Wentz-led offense. The running game was in bad shape as Aaron Jones had just 10 yards on three carries.

An endzone interception of Josh Allen by Byron Murphy helped to lift spirits in the Twin Cities, but O'Connell's team trailed 10-3 heading into the locker room at halftime.
